name: Maz Repository
observations: GitHub repo Mazoo85/maz
Holds two things: the Maz Engine (native C++ game engine) and ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE (browser game)
Root README.md documents both projects

name: Maz Engine
observations: Native C++20 + Vulkan + SDL3 game engine
2D-first but architected so 3D drops in later (renderer interface, camera abstraction, scene graph)
Built with CMake >= 3.24, warnings-as-errors; SDL3 and GLM fetched automatically via FetchContent
Current milestone is M0: the walking skeleton (window, fixed-timestep loop, Vulkan clear-screen renderer, clean shutdown)
Degrades gracefully with no GPU/display so it runs headless in CI
Lives under engine/ with core/, platform/, math/, render/ modules
Demo app is apps/sandbox; supports --headless and --frames N flags
Design docs: docs/ROADMAP.md (14-phase plan) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

name: ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE
observations: Browser-playable Project Zomboid-style open-world zombie survival game
Rendered as a 1990s SEGA 16-bit neon arcade title
Pure HTML5 Canvas + vanilla JavaScript, no build step or dependencies
Map is a 160x140 tile replica of downtown & midtown Anchorage, Alaska with real street and building names
Entry point is index.html; can also run via python3 -m http.server
Is the engine's eventual Phase 13 native-port target and design reference

name: ZOMBOID source layout
observations: index.html: shell + script load order
css/style.css: arcade-cabinet styling, scanlines
js/world.js: Anchorage data (avenues, streets, named buildings)
js/worldgen.js: bakes data into a tile grid + loot containers
js/items.js: item definitions + themed loot tables
js/audio.js: WebAudio chiptune SFX + music
js/game.js: engine (states, input, sim, combat, rendering, HUD)

name: Codebase Memory MCP
observations: MCP server that gives Claude persistent, cross-session memory about this codebase
Configured in .mcp.json as server name codebase-memory
Uses the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory package via npx
Launched through scripts/codebase-memory-server.sh, which pins the memory file to an absolute path in the repo
Knowledge graph is stored at .claude/codebase-memory.json and committed to git
Documented in docs/CODEBASE_MEMORY.md

name: Zomboid Native Port
observations: Native C++20 port of the ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE browser game's deterministic simulation onto Maz Engine (roadmap Phase 13)
Lives in game/ as the dependency-free static library target 'zomboid' (alias maz::zomboid) — no SDL3/Vulkan/GLM, so it compiles and unit-tests headless in CI with no GPU/display

Public headers under game/include/zomboid/: Math.hpp (Vec2 + clamp/lerp/dist/normAngle), Rng.hpp (PCG32 deterministic RNG replacing JS Math.random()), Tiles.hpp (Tile enum + isSolidTile), World.hpp, Items.hpp, Sim.hpp
Sources under game/src/: World.cpp (Anchorage avenues/streets/buildings data + generateWorld), Items.cpp (item DB + themed weighted loot tables + rollLoot), Sim.cpp (the fixed-timestep simulation)

Sim is driven by a per-tick zb::Input intent struct (moveX/moveY, aim, attackHeld/attackPressed, interact, reload, useSlot, toggleFlashlight); step() runs updatePlayer/updateZombies/updateBullets/updateWorld at fixed kStep=1/60

Faithfully ports: five decaying needs (health/hunger/thirst/fatigue/mood), infection + bite chance, melee arc combat with weapon durability/breakage, ranged pistol/shotgun with ammo + bullets, zombie sight/wander/knockback AI + sprinters, day/night cycle with day-scaled night wave spawning, richness-scaled building loot containers
Purely-visual reference state (particles, float-texts, screen shake, CRT/scanline post-fx) is intentionally excluded from the sim and deferred to the future render layer
Documented in docs/ZOMBOID_PORT.md; design mapping table links each js/ file to its game/ counterpart

Has a dependency-free software reference rasterizer under game/include/zomboid/render/: Framebuffer.hpp (CPU RGB buffer with fill/blend/outline/circle/thick-line) and SoftRenderer.hpp/.cpp (renderScene() game viewport + renderWorldMap() overview) using the neon SEGA palette; deterministic and unit-tested (render check in zomboid_tests)

apps/zomboid gained a --render out.png mode (with --map/--width/--height/--tile) that writes a PNG via a tiny built-in stored-DEFLATE encoder in apps/zomboid/Png.hpp — lets the port be seen with no GPU; verified frames show the Anchorage street grid, purple-walled buildings with orange loot crates, trees, player + zombies

Code is clean under both g++ and clang with -Wconversion AND -Wsign-conversion -Werror (clang's -Wconversion implies sign-conversion); the software renderer defines the exact draw intent the future Vulkan sprite batch will reproduce and seeds Phase 12 golden-image tests

name: zomboid headless driver
observations: apps/zomboid/main.cpp — headless autopilot executable (CMake target zomboid_game, output name 'zomboid')

Runs the ported Sim with a built-in autopilot that aims at the nearest zombie, backs away from close threats, swings, and periodically loots; prints a run summary (day/time, needs, kills, z-alive, weapon)
Flags: --ticks N, --seed S, --quiet, --help
Proof-of-life for the native port; a windowed renderer will bridge onto the same Sim later

name: zomboid unit tests
observations: tests/zomboid_tests.cpp — dependency-free unit tests for the Zomboid sim, wired as ctest 'zomboid_sim_tests' (links maz::zomboid)
Self-contained CHECK harness (no framework); exits non-zero on failure

Covers worldgen invariants + determinism, seeded reproducibility, starting kit, needs decay (thirst outpaces hunger), consumable eating, melee combat kills, loot roll counts + default-table fallback, day/night darkness range
Verified locally under -Werror with g++ 13: 36 checks, 0 failures
